# NOLX verification and POSIX conformance dashboard

**Generated by `tools/conformance-report.py` from `docs/testing/assertions/`. Do not edit by hand.**

_Generated from 416 assertions._

This dashboard is a coverage record, not a conformance certificate. It includes POSIX specification assertions and platform bring-up assertions; only POSIX areas make POSIX conformance claims. Each row shows what is implemented and what test backs it. See [conformance.md](conformance.md) for the status definitions.

| MM-029 | mm | Page tables in the kernel: per-process address spaces are built over frames from the allocator | `tested-T2` | `AddressSpace::create_in_place` takes a zeroed PML4 from the frame allocator, marks it a page table, charges the system PTE pool, and shares the kernel half of the address space by copying the running root's PML4 entries from slot 256 up; everything below that is allocated and reclaimed by kernel/src/mm/tables.rs `KernelTableStore`, whose `release_table` returns an empty table to the frame allocator and releases its pool charge. The space is built *in place*, one field at a time, and torn down through a borrow: a value of the type is tens of kilobytes -- the boot self test found a stack overflow that had been silently writing past the kernel stack -- so nothing may move one through a function boundary. Teardown unmaps every range, frees the child tables the unmaps emptied, and frees the PML4. The boot self test proves the accounting closes: the page-table allocate/release counters move by the same amount across the test and the free-frame count returns to exactly its pre-test value, which is the `free frames A -> A; page tables allocated X -> Y, released X -> Y` part of the boot smoke's address-space assertion. (CI run 38125065287, revision 2e7279b) |

| MM-032 | mm | Demand paging and copy-on-write: the four fault causes resolve against the VAD tree and the commit charge | `tested-T2` | kernel/src/mm/space::resolve implements the four causes of docs/architecture/03-memory-manager.md -- demand zero on a committed private page (the frame is zeroed before it is mapped and the test reads the zeroes back through the direct map), copy on write of a shared read-only page (`share_into` makes both spaces point at one frame read-only with a refcount of two; the child's write copies the frame, the copy carries the parent's byte, the two sides then move independently, and a write with no other owner re-protects in place instead of copying), a file-backed range refused until the Cache Manager exists (M7), and stack growth that extends a grow-down VAD by one page, coalesces the new descriptor back into the stack's own, demand-zeroes the new page, and refuses below the space's floor or beyond the growth limit -- and refuses an access in no VAD, a write to an `mprotect(PROT_READ)` page (a protection violation, not a copy), a fault on a guard page, and anything in the kernel half. kernel/src/hal/interrupts.rs routes vector 14 to it before the fatal report, so a resolvable fault returns to the faulting instruction. Six host tests cover it. The kernel builds one node over the frames the frame map describes (`kernel/src/mm/numa.rs`), reports `mm: numa: 1 node(s), ..., local node 0, 121701 free frames, zonelist [0], distance matrix local=10`, and `mm::allocate_frames` now chooses the node by walking that zonelist before it allocates -- with one node that is one iteration, and a node that has no allocator refuses instead of taking memory from the wrong node. Local evidence: Q35 and PC with QEMU 11.1.50, 120 481 and 120 609 frames taken and returned, `free frames ... -> ...` exact, audit ok. CI evidence: run [39593547832](https://github.com/NeXuS4Dev/NOLX/actions/runs/39593547832) on revision `10d738a`, job *Native USB HID interrupts, lifecycle and DMA safety*, step *Verify an empty frame allocator and a full kernel heap refuse instead of corrupting*. | |
| MM-036 | mm | Kernel heap exhaustion and over-aligned blocks: a request no region may serve is refused, live over-aligned payloads stay intact, and bytes-in-use return to their starting value | `tested-T2` | Same fixture. It allocates 1 MiB blocks aligned to a page until the heap's 16-region cap refuses, fills every block so overlapping ownership would be visible, re-reads every block to prove the payload survived, requires an 8 MiB request (larger than the 4 MiB ceiling on one region) to return null, and requires `bytes_in_use` to return to exactly the value it found, with the heap's own metadata check and `mm::audit` passing afterwards. This fixture found two real defects in the heap's over-aligned path, both fixed in `kernel/src/mm/heap.rs`: the two bookkeeping words were written *at* the returned pointer instead of in front of it, so the caller's first write destroyed them and the block could never be freed (`HEAP CORRUPTION: the payload offset is not inside the region`), and the reservation omitted those words, so the caller's last eight bytes landed on the next block's header. A region is now also skipped for any request larger than the region itself, so a damaged free-list entry cannot make an impossible request look servable. Local evidence: PC and Q35, 37 blocks served across 16 regions, refusal, release, `in use 0 -> 0 bytes`, audit ok. CI evidence: the same run and step as MM-035. | |

Locally the xHCI fixture passed on PC and Q35 too. Executable fixtures now cover the three previously missing kinds. `scripts/check-xhci-lifecycle.py --mode exhaust` with `hal-xhci-exhaust-test` stops the enumerated controller, takes all 128 candidates of the xHCI pool for a synthetic owner, requires the start to be refused as `NoVector` with unchanged DMA/MMIO and no stolen claim, then releases the pool and requires the restart to reacquire a vector, with removal returning every page. `scripts/check-e1000-recovery.py` with `hal-e1000-recovery-test` exhausts the shared INTx pool and distinguishes the refusal as `RouteError::NoVector` (no route reference, no DMA/MMIO leak); `scripts/check-virtio-net-recovery.py` with `hal-virtio-net-recovery-test` exhausts both RX and TX pools and requires the pair to be reclaimed. The storage fixtures (`check-ahci-nvme-recovery.py`, `check-virtio-blk-recovery.py`) already covered AHCI/NVMe/virtio-blk, and the shared rules passed host tests in CI [39391895780](https://github.com/NeXuS4Dev/NOLX/actions/runs/39391895780). The xHCI exhaust fixture passed locally on Q35 with QEMU 11.1.50 (128 candidates, refusal, reacquisition, final DMA 0) and in CI run [39593547832](https://github.com/NeXuS4Dev/NOLX/actions/runs/39593547832) on revision `10d738a`. The network fixtures need QEMU's user-mode network backend, which this sandbox's portable build lacks; in CI they run first in their job, and their e1000 half currently fails at `recovery.rs:180` (`driver_start::start` → `OpFailed` after a checked stop) for reasons recorded in `docs/development/m9-completion.md` — a regression that predates this checkpoint, not a failure of the exhaustion phase. Status stays `pending-T2` until that run passes. |
